questions.q: Why did the Renaissance begin in Italy in the 14th century?
questions.answer: (1) Italy was divided into small city states at that time. The geographical position of Italian cities made them great trading and intellectual centers. Many great ideas, along with wealth, were brought by merchants from far corners of the globe. (2) These states had political freedom, and new commercial techniques like book-keeping and bills of exchange made Italy prosperous, giving people leisure for study and art.

questions.q: Why was the Glorious Revolution of 1688 called 'glorious'? Why did King James II lose the support of his countrymen?
questions.answer: (1) It was called the Glorious Revolution because no blood was shed to achieve its success. (2) The Stuart king James II lost the popular support of his countrymen. This was due to his harsh attitude towards the people. The creation of an expensive standing army and increasing employment of Roman Catholics in the government, army and universities had angered the people. (3) The Parliament removed King James II from the throne in favor of his daughter Mary II and her husband William III, Prince of Orange. The autocratic rule of James II was replaced with a constitutional form of government.

questions.answer: (1) Michael Servetus, a Spanish doctor, discovered the circulation of blood. (2) William Harvey, an Englishman explained the function of the heart in purifying blood and its circulation through veins.

questions.q: Mention any two accomplishments in astronomy during the Renaissance.
questions.answer: (1) Copernicus in his book On the Revolution of the Heavenly Sphere argued that the earth and the planets move around the sun in concentric circles. (2) Kepler further developed this theory and said that the other planets move in elliptical paths around the sun. With his self manufactured telescope, Galileo discovered the moons of Jupiter, the rings of Saturn and spots in the Sun.

questions.q: Explain any six major causes of the Russian Revolution.
questions.answer: (1) Tsar was an autocratic and oppressive ruler; hence the workers and the peasants suffered a lot. People were also denied any political rights. The nobility were also dissatisfied with Tsar Nicholas II due to his autocratic ways. (2) Exploitation along with inhuman working conditions and huge amount of taxes had made the people rise against him. (3) Famines further worsened the situation in the country. The army lacked ammunition, the cities lacked food while the peasants failed to get proper return for their produce. (4) Russia had also entered World War I for imperialist gains. Thousands of Russian soldiers were killed in World War I as they were ill equipped with no proper warm uniforms and arms to fight in the cold desert of Siberia. (5) The government in the meantime had printed millions of Rouble notes leading to inflation. (6) This situation was further worsened by the writings of Marx and Tolstoy which influenced the people, especially the workers, and led to their political awakening. In February 1917, Tsar was deposed and a Provisional Government was established under the Another Party called the Bolshevik headed by Lenin organised the Soviets and replaced the Government in October 1917.

or.q: Explain the socialist movement and its impact on Russia in six points.
or.answer: (1) The Industrial Revolution had led to an unequal society. It created a class of industrial workers/proletariat who were miserably exploited by the capitalists/bourgeoisie. (2) It aimed to reduce corruption as well as to improve and strengthen Catholic Church. The idea of socialism, which tries to establish equal society, began to take root. (3) The most powerful and influential ideas of socialism was given by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. In the book Das Capital, Marx pointed out that history of all societies is the history of class struggle. (4) The Pope established their own political rule in what were called the Papal States. He predicted that the struggle will be successful with the end of capitalism and the coming of socialism. This will result in the control of the ownership of the means of production in the hands of the state and the birth of an equal society. (5) It showed that the Parliament had the power to change the monarch. This led to the formation of the Council of Workers called the Soviets. The Russian Revolution was inspired by the ideology of socialism. (6) The first practical example of this was the Russian revolution which resulted in the establishment of the first socialist government of the world. Another Party called the Bolshevik headed by Lenin organised the Soviets and replaced the Government in October 1917.
